title: Meta Puts Muse In Your Pocket, Google Ships AI to Orbit & Oracle's Data Center Bet Wobbles
sources: The Neuron, The Rundown AI, Morning Brew, 1440 Daily Digest (Sep 25)
tldr: Meta's pocket AI device "Muse Charm" ships in December with glasses integration coming soon — a hardware race worth tracking if you advise on AI UX.
Oracle may delay payments on its $165B "Project Jupiter" AI data center over permitting fights — a real signal of strain in the AI infrastructure buildout.
Mortgage rates just hit 7% for the first time since January 2025 — a good prompt to revisit any client budgeting assumptions built on cheaper borrowing.

tips.heading: Turn a Google Sheet into an interactive dashboard with Gemini Canvas
steps: Open the spreadsheet you want to visualize (e.g. a project tracker or content calendar) in Google Sheets.
Launch Gemini in a new tab, click the + button, and select Canvas.
Prompt Gemini with the template below to build the dashboard from your data.
Copy the Canvas link to view or share it outside the chat — edits you make later update live for anyone with the link.
tips.prompt: Make me an interactive dashboard using the data from tabs one and two

tips.heading: Audit your AI tool's instructions before they quietly wreck your outputs
steps: Gather every instruction file, outline, or feedback note you've fed the AI over time.
Have the AI flag duplicated, conflicting, or outdated rules, citing the specific files.
Review its proposal and decide what to keep, archive, or rewrite — approve before anything is edited.
Keep the surviving set lean (e.g. one structure guide + one voice guide) instead of stacking every draft version.
tips.prompt: Review the instructions and examples in [project/folder]. Identify duplicated, conflicting, and outdated rules, citing the specific files and short excerpts. Propose what to keep, archive, or rewrite. Do not modify files until I approve.

news.body: Meta unveiled "Muse Charm," a pocket AI-agent device, plus Muse integration into Ray-Ban glasses — announced at Meta Connect and shipping December. New Muse partners include PayPal, Walmart, Shopify, GitHub, and Box.
news.means: Meta is betting AI agents belong on your body, not just your phone. Worth watching as a UX reference point if you're scoping AI hardware or agent-assistant features for clients.

news.body: Oracle warned it may delay payments on its $165B "Project Jupiter" AI data center if the project isn't operational by 2028 — a key natural-gas pipeline permit keeps getting denied amid local opposition. Oracle stock fell ~3.5% on the news; the project's debt is trading at 90 cents on the dollar.
news.means: A concrete example of AI infrastructure spending running into real-world permitting and financing friction — a useful, specific data point for any client conversation about AI capex timelines.

news.body: The White House reportedly asked OpenAI and Anthropic to withhold new frontier models from U.K. testers until the U.S. government reviews them first.
news.means: A concrete first move toward the U.S. asserting review authority over frontier model releases — worth flagging if you track AI governance for clients with multinational AI rollouts.

beyond_ai.body: Trump hosted Xi Jinping for Oval Office talks and a state dinner, with AI, Iran, and Taiwan on the agenda; OpenAI's Sam Altman, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and Google's Sundar Pichai were among the guests. Separately, a federal judge restored White House press access for CNN, MS NOW, and Politico after a ban.
beyond_ai.angle: Top AI executives sitting at a US-China state dinner underscores how central AI policy now is to great-power diplomacy — relevant context for any client work touching trade, supply chain, or cross-border AI deployment.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you catch that Altman, Huang, and Pichai were all at the Xi state dinner? AI's fully a geopolitical chess piece now.

beyond_ai.body: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate hit 7.03%, its highest since January 2025, as the 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5% amid inflation and oil-price pressure from the Iran conflict.
beyond_ai.angle: Directly relevant — any client budgeting or real-estate planning that assumed cheaper borrowing this quarter should be revisited now.
beyond_ai.starter: Are we still planning around lower borrowing costs, or should we push that assumption out given rates just hit 7%?

beyond_ai.body: New York's gambling regulator sued Polymarket US for operating without a license, following a similar suit against Kalshi two months ago; Polymarket argues prediction markets fall under federal, not state, jurisdiction.
beyond_ai.angle: A live state-vs-federal jurisdiction fight worth knowing if you have fintech or prediction-market-adjacent clients watching regulatory arbitrage.
beyond_ai.starter: Have you been following the Polymarket/Kalshi gambling-law fights? Could reshape how prediction markets operate state by state.

beyond_ai.body: Starbucks is closing 250 more North American stores, on top of 627 closed last year, as part of an ongoing footprint rationalization.
beyond_ai.angle: A useful current case study if you're advising retail or restaurant clients on store-footprint and cost-structure decisions.
beyond_ai.starter: Starbucks just closed another 250 stores — anyone else seeing more retail clients quietly right-sizing their footprint this year?

beyond_ai.body: Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek's new memoir claims successor Bob Iger ran a "three-year campaign" to push him out before his 2022 ouster; Disney insiders call the account revisionist.
beyond_ai.angle: A vivid, recognizable case study in CEO succession failure and board governance — good material if you do leadership or transition-planning work.
beyond_ai.starter: Have you read about the Chapek-Iger memoir feud? It's a pretty stark example of how badly a CEO succession can go sideways.
